name: strace
description: Traces the system calls a program makes: every file open, network connection, and memory operation, live.

flags.description: Write the trace to a file.
Filter: file, network, memory, or specific calls (open,read).
Summary: count and time per syscall.
Show time spent in each call.

examples.explanation: Reveals exactly which files ls opens — the fastest answer to "where does this program read its config from?".
Summary mode: which system calls dominate the runtime.
Watches a running process's network activity live — invaluable for "what is this process connecting to?".

about: strace intercepts syscalls via ptrace. It shows the raw truth of what a program does: failed file opens (ENOACC), DNS lookups, connect() targets. Slows programs significantly — never use in production hot paths, always for diagnosis.
useCases: Find which config file a program actually reads.
See what a mystery binary connects to.
mistakes: Running strace on setuid binaries expecting elevated tracing (kernel drops privileges first).
Using it in production performance analysis without accounting for its overhead.
